notes.title: Steam Awards! Achievements and Changelog 1.1.10
notes.content:
Hi guys!
We hope you're enjoying the current and upcoming promotions on Steam! As usual, we have prepared another patch for you, as described below, and now we would like to invite you to take part in the annual nomination of games for [b]Steam Awards[/b]! 
This year we have the pleasure of competing with other titles in the "[b]Sit back and relax[/b]" category, which probably best describes your experience with Tribe: Primitive Builder!

We will be grateful for every vote, it means world to us! In the meantime, we invite you once again to take part in the autumn sale and a trip to a "desert" island in Tribe: Primitive Builder!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34986580/c07c689007963287a68f24f1b4eeafe57c686956.png[/img]
[h3]Changelog 1.1.10:[/h3]
1. Gameplay:
[list]
[*] Changed the location of the village's main warehouse to a more suitable place under the new village main bonfires
[*] There are now salvageable ruins in the old underground warehouse
[*] Moved Elder's favorite locations to new places near bonfires, stockpiles and the altar.
[*] The Elder is much faster now
[*] All of the above changes open players up to new locations and make building in other places more convenient. There are also many fewer miles to travel from one quest-spot to the next because the Elder is in places that are easier to get to.
[/list]
2. Achievements:
[list]
[*] Added the first iteration of Steam Achievements
[*] You are welcome to post your propositions for the next pack
[/list]
3. Small optimization changes as well as new routes for tribesmen and player to use

[h3]Changelog 1.1.8 that you might have missed: [/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34986580/1021bcaffaed43624046a2b74b341d35d63736ff.gif[/img]

[list]
[*]Automated change of the production takes place when the previous one is completed or 2 seconds after pausing production for any reason. 
[*]The distance from resources still counts so it's not wise to make a queue for everything, just pick resources in your gatherer's hut that are nearby.
[*]If you want to speed up production even more and you hired full crew in the building already, just build another hut of the same kind.
[/list]

tags.balance_change: The Elder is much faster now

notes.title: Tribe: Primitive Builder Changelog 1.1.5
notes.content:
Hi guys, 
here's the changelog for the 1.1.5 release, thank you for your support and requests to make Tribe: Primitive Builder the best game possible!

[olist]
[*]In response to feedback about building management issues, we added:
[list]
[*] The ability to change the names of buildings in the tribe panel.
[*] Drag and drop functionality for buildings in the tribe panel, allowing you to rearrange their display order in any tab.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34986580/5c35872c57df3158a729c883e154da0cfa248862.gif[/img]
[*] The ability to view the inventory of all storages and marketplaces when you enter one of them, with left and right arrows next to the building's name.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34986580/8e96ac5ea88cb693e1e426d89eb2c0750f31d738.gif[/img]

[/list]
[*]In response to feedback about the difficulty of gathering enough leather in the Sand Land, we added:
[list]
[*] Hawk's Eye now highlights animals within its range for its entire duration.
[*] There are more animals nearby the SandLand's Altar
[/list][previewyoutube=TkbV8Z-9K6Q;full][/previewyoutube]

[*]In response to feedback about the long distances to travel in the Grass Land when completing early quests, we added:
[list]
[*]A new location for tribesmen to spend time near the Altar's cave. 
Tribesmen will be able to travel and stay there already [b]in the next[/b] patches. It shouldn't collide with buildings built by players, if so, please let us know or use your hammer to disassemble that hut and move it to another location. You can also keep playing the old version "1.1.3" available in the "Betas" tab of the Steam app (choose "old-version-1.1.3" branch).
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34986580/5cc432f661ad554f21865f6b20cf015264c7b61d.jpg[/img]
[*]Many new spawn points of herbs and sticks needed for rituals along the entrance path to the Altar's cave.
[*]Added an auto-run option, with the default key being ']' (customizable in the options).
[*]Added a workshop next to the first Altar in the Altar's cave, allowing players to craft items without returning to the starting location.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34986580/2bf759333e6d5c1a8d3d5c5694e362c9a28b14d5.jpg[/img]  

[/list]
[*]Bug fixes and minor changes:
[list]
[*]Mouse wheel assignment in the keybindings now works correctly - keep the cursor over the key assignment field and click or scroll to assign mouse button.
[*] The Split window no longer closes when a new item appears in storage or the backpack, unless changes in the backpack make splitting impossible.
[*] Every few days, sleeping forces an additional respawn of resources, regardless of distances from player.
[*] Fixed several places where players could get stuck between rocks.
[*] Animals will no longer get stuck on their territory boundary.
[*] Campfires near the Grass Land Altar now have the correct sound and lighting.
[*] Food quantity and other info in the Tribe Panel under the Storages tab refreshes correctly now.
[*] Improved and optimized culling distances for many objects in all Lands.
[*] Improved the appearance of ponds in the Stone Land.
[*] Improved the appearance of the inhabited area in the Volcano Land.
[*] Fixed crash when loading bridge scaffold when in was built in a specific way
[*] Added a marker for an empty space in the Ocean Gate area as part of the Build a Marketplace quest.
[/list]
[/olist]
[h2]Steam Input configuration (Controller Support) [/h2]
Steam Input configuration is an optional solution for a lack of controller support. It is a setup designed to function as a keyboard layout binding.

You can use it as is, or you can consider it as a base template to set up your own configuration.
Here's a quick guide:
[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34986580/b43f2cd0ad11965b5ba5a7b1f82a67244bd86a3e.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34986580/386b34bf31f66f373071247fa08a9413a4368e0f.png[/img][/url]

notes.title: Patch 1.1.2 including your requests from the recent reviews
notes.content:
[h1]Welcome fellow tribesman![/h1] 
Today's patch is the outcome of your Steam forum requests and comments in the reviews. We've read them all and decided to give it a try and propose significant changes to your [b]Storages[/b] and [b]Marketplaces[/b] so that managing villages becomes more convenient and intuitive. 

Here are bullet points to keep it simple:

[olist]
[*]All of your storage huts (and the main [b]Village storage[/b]) in the same biom (Sand land, Stone land etc.) are now linked together automatically, that means:
[list]
[*]You can automate the production of food in the '[b]Village storage[/b]', than build another separate '[b]Storage Hut[/b]' that will provide food to your linked huts right away using resources from the '[b]Village storage[/b]'
[*]You still need to take care of Carriers and hire enough employees, but you are no longer limited by max 15 buildings linked to one '[b]Storage Hut[/b]' 
[/list]
[*][b]'Storage hut'[/b] no longer needs to be linked to [b]'Marketplaces'[/b] in the same biom.
[list]
[*]Each [b]'Marketplace'[/b] has an access to all of the [b]'Storage huts'[/b] and vice versa in the same biom
[*]You are no longer limited to link only 5 resources to a village in another land - you can build a second [b]'Marketplace'[/b], hire carriers and send more resources  
[/list][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34986580/b894ebea7a7dd770bb5cbb820ff05fc288664d83.jpg[/img]
[*]From now on, you can send to other [b]'Marketplaces'[/b] not only resources but Tools as well (Knives, Axes etc.).[list]
[*]Added an option to restrict amount of each item you send between [b]'Marketplaces"[/b] instead of using only global settings (so that Carriers leave certain amount of each resource you choose in storage)
[*]Added an option to restrict maximum amount of a resource to keep in the destination place (so that Marketplaces in other Lands won't be flooded with hammers if you only need a few there).
[/list][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34986580/2f2b896cf0e94bc016091473b604873c01549cc3.png[/img][/olist]
Thank you once again for every inquire on Steam, [url=https://discord.gg/gHb5XtURgr]Discord[/url] and Google surveys. We've managed to release almost 20 patches of smaller and bigger changes from the initial release. The game is more stable and complete thanks to you!

tags.feature: All of your storage huts (and the main Village storage) in the same biom (Sand land, Stone land etc.) are now linked together automatically, that means:

You can automate the production of food in the 'Village storage', than build another separate 'Storage Hut' that will provide food to your linked huts right away using resources from the 'Village storage'
You still need to take care of Carriers and hire enough employees, but you are no longer limited by max 15 buildings linked to one 'Storage Hut'
'Storage hut' no longer needs to be linked to 'Marketplaces' in the same biom.
Each 'Marketplace' has an access to all of the 'Storage huts' and vice versa in the same biom
You are no longer limited to link only 5 resources to a village in another land - you can build a second 'Marketplace', hire carriers and send more resources
From now on, you can send to other 'Marketplaces' not only resources but Tools as well (Knives, Axes etc.).
Added an option to restrict amount of each item you send between 'Marketplaces" instead of using only global settings (so that Carriers leave certain amount of each resource you choose in storage)
Added an option to restrict maximum amount of a resource to keep in the destination place (so that Marketplaces in other Lands won't be flooded with hammers if you only need a few there).

notes.title: Changelog for Tribe Version 0.6.10
notes.content:
Changelog for Tribe Version 0.6.10:
[list]
[*] Added the ability to change production from the tribe panel.
[*] Mouse scroll can switch equipped tools in quick slots (as long as you're not in the process of building a structure) + key bindings (Equip Next Tool, Equip Previous Tool).
[*] When a tool in your quick bar is used up and you have another one in your inventory, it will be automatically replaced in quick bar with the next available tool.
[*] Pinned building costs may remain on the screen even after finishing the construction; they should now disappear automatically.
[*] Holding Q to open the menu and then immediately closing it has been fixed; it should only close upon release or if pressed a second time.
[*] The sound of building destruction no longer plays multiple times, which was giving the impression of being very loud.
[*] Reduced energy cost for construction actions by 30%.
[*] Reduced energy cost for gathering actions by 25%.
[*] Rapidly swinging tools without a target no longer consumes player's energy.
[*] Replaced the spear icon with a more stone-like one.
[*] Excluded invisible sphere-related fish spawn reflections from affecting the game's overall reflection.
[*] Added a loading screen tip: You can pin a full list of resources needed for buildings, rituals, or tools to the HUD using the middle mouse button.
[*] Fixed the visible box from the campfire with the natives.
[*] Improved dialogue font to support all languages (encoding) + handling of special German and Polish characters.
[*] Estimated wake-up time correctly displays 12 am and 12 pm.
[*] Unstuck for fellow tribesmen.
[*] -- Resolves the issue of falling under the ground after loading the game in rare cases.
[*] Increased distances from which you can build Cook's Fisherman's, Gatherer's, Witch, and Toolmaker Huts.
[*] Fixed Sand Land triggering in Grass Land (in lava right next to the bridge).
[*] More precise detection of Stone Land areas.
[*] Another musical theme.
[*] Rabbits and raccoons move on RM, 5-second freeze fix, improvements in BTT trees and detection/perception.
[*] Spear: Adjusted insertion socket (easier to remove when rotated), fixed fish interactions (received adjustments to avoid getting stuck in the ground or rotating endlessly).
[*] Proper removal of nonexistent animal instances.
[/list]

notes.title: Play Tribe Primitive Builder Playtest v2
notes.content:
We invite you to play Tribe Primitive Builder Playtest v2!

[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1059900/Tribe_Primitive_Builder/][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34986580/77a230408667478075fd66464fc64027c31b7ffa.png[/img][/url]

Remember also about the competition we wrote about here:
https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1059900/view/3686812408423764830

We wish you a lot of fun!

Below is a list of new things that await you in the game:

Automation:
[list]
[*] The village warehouse allow you to hire carriers who make sure that all buildings that are connected to it have access to their chests and the warehouse chest
[*] 2 new quests + 2 tutorials in Grass Land introducing the player to the mechanics of automation
[*] Ritual unlocking the Storage Hut building, allowing you to chain together up to 15 buildings at once
[/list]

Transporting resources between map tiers (e.g. Grass Land -> Sand Land):
[list]
[*] The appropriate ritual unlocks the construction of the market
[*] We assign any number of warehouses to the market, from which it will take resources
[*] We are setting a trade route to the next market, every 5 minutes selected resources will be transported between markets
[*] Necessary to explore more lands where some resources are not available to collect
[*] 
[/list]

The new Tribe Panel allows you to:
[list]
[*] Change of employment in production huts
[*] Assigning huts to warehouses
[*] Assign warehouses to markets
[*] Defining trade routes
[/list]

Map Changes:
[list]
[*] You can now place your own markers
[*] Visualization of connections between huts and warehouses, warehouses with markets and trade routes
[*] You can see buildings under construction
[*] Rituals to unlock fast travel between altars in different Lands (Grass Land, Sand Land, Stone Land, Volcanic Land)
[/list]

Weather:
[list]
[*] weather conditions change:
[*] -- during the game after the time runs out, they are also dependent on the Land
[*] -- in Sand Land it will rain, in Grass Land there will be no sandstorm, etc.
[*] weather: heavy rain/sandstorm, light rain/sandstorm, cloudy, more cloudy, clear sky,
[/list]

Sounds:
[list]
[*] NPC voice acting
[*] In-game music (every 6 tracks)
[*] Completed many missing sounds
[/list]

New buildings to build in Grass Land (after performing the appropriate rituals):
[list]
[*] Marketplace
[*] Storage Hut
[*] Tool Maker's Hut
[*] Ruins:
[*] The remains of old buildings are scattered around the map
[*] They contain chests that the player can loot
[*] They can be destroyed with a hammer, recovering some of the resources
[*] Tutorial about building salvage when the player equips the hammer
[*] 
[/list]

Production bonuses:
[list]
[*] The player can find small shrines hidden on the map that increase the production of specific resources in his tribe
[*] After completing an appropriate ritual, the player can create better quality totems and replace them in huts with workers, increasing their production output
[*] -- Only Wooden Totem Ritual available in Grass Land, Clay Totem, Stone Totem, Obsidian Totem in other lands
[/list]

Fraction:
[list]
[*] All buildings can now be smashed with a hammer
[/list]

Optimization:
[list]
[*] For high settings: depending on the machine + fps
[*] Reducing the size of save files by 90%
[/list]

Smaller interesting or player-requested changes:
[list]
[*] Pin blueprints to HUD (buildings, items, rituals)
[*] Changes in quests so that the player doesn't have to run to the Altar twice in the beginning of the game
[*] In the Workshop and Sleep Hut buildings, they now hang with a bead that the player and NPC push
[*] 500+ smaller changes/fixes
[/list]

In addition, things that players will not have access to during playtests (spoiler warning):
[list]
[*] Two new ready-made areas: Sand Land, Ocean Gate
[*] Two new areas in progress: Stone Land, Volcanic Land
[*] About 20 new quests in other Lands besides the starting one
[*] New special buildings in the next Lands
[*] New huts to build
[/list]

notes.title: Devlog #5: Struggles with nature
notes.content:
[h3]Hello again, and welcome to the next Tribe: Primitive Builder devlog![/h3]

This time we'll be talking about ways that players will struggle to survive on an island, our approach to combat, and the effects of weather.

From the day we decided to start working on Tribe, our goal was to make something unique. While still taking inspiration from other similar titles, we wanted to refresh a little bit the survival/simulator formula. To achieve this, we made some critical decisions for our game design. One of them was that the player wouldn't be alone on this island; there will be lots of NPC characters in the form of village members that will be working with the player towards the common goal of surviving. We wanted players to be a part of a growing community and to play a very specific and important role in the development of the tribe. Because of that, we also decided that players won't be able to do everything alone and will need to rely a little bit on other tribe members. That’s why we decided that the role our players will play in this primitive society is to build and explore the island, to innovate and communicate with gods. All of this makes players responsible for prosperity and how fast this society will develop. This is already quite a lot of work to do, so we decided that more mundane tasks will be fulfilled by other tribe members. Thus, the roles played by NPCs are Hunters, Fishermen, Farmers, etc. Players will still be able to collect some food, though mostly from fruit bushes.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34986580/0d03e77e1a652d2db182e38db1621251b3931073.png[/img]

Another decision was that we wanted to create a relaxing experience focused on constructing, exploring, and interacting with the culture of the players' tribe. The big consequence of this decision is that we decided that there won't be any hostile creatures on the island: by this, we mean there’s no dangerous animals, and no hostile tribes. We wanted to encourage players to explore more, and the lack of threats during the day worked well with that idea in mind. The lack of hostility between tribe members is also important, as all inhabitants of this island are descendants of one tribe that the player is part of and plays an important role in. During the late game there can be some misunderstandings between subtribes that could escalate to a temporary split from the main tribe, but it will never lead to bloodshed. No matter how angry our tribesmen are, they don't believe violence is an answer. Their beliefs are concentrated about balance in nature; cycles of day and night, rainstorms that will always turn into clear skies, the circle of life and death that comes naturally. All of this is reflected not only in their behaviour but also on their bodies, with light colored paintings in front and dark patterns on their backs. Since the player character also follows this set of beliefs, we decided to remove the ability to hit NPC characters with tools. The reason being that during the tests of our game, we noticed that players will try to hit NPC characters, and when they discovered that it was possible, the next step for them was to try to kill them. The penalty of losing reputation and, in the end, losing the game was not enough to stop them from doing this. Because this "game over" screen and reloading to the last save point was only stalling the player experience, we made a decision to remove the feature from the final game. Now players will need to start thinking the same way as their character and find solutions to conflicts outside of resorting to brute strength.


Although, there will still be other things that can catch careless players off guard!

As we said, we wanted players to explore during the day, when the island is warm and cozy. But at night... Well, that’s a different story altogether. Many primitive tribes feared the night, and the unknown that could hide in the darkness. As there are no monsters on the island (as far as we know), there is something equally dangerous. Nights on our tropical island can get devastatingly cold, and players that are far from the village could risk freezing to death. To avoid this from happening, players can construct temporary camps that require only a small amount of resources and will provide them with a fireplace and a place to sleep. As you already know, sleeping in a village is important because it allows you to discover new things, but we also wanted to allow players to skip night whilst out in the wild, looking for those unique places and sparks of imagination. Just don't wait to construct them at the last moment, nights can get really dark! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34986580/469d258c4d4b49099ad01cb6f2a467e95c33f6f9.png[/img]

There will also be times that during the day the island will be consumed by powerful rainstorms. Seeking shelter during these will also be important. Players won't be losing temperature as quickly as during the night, but it could also be lethal. Keep in mind that rainstorms will affect not only players, but also the whole Tribe. If some of your constructions were already in poor condition, you could find that some of them collapsed completely, leaving some of your fellow tribesmen homeless and without work. This will have severe consequences on the prosperity of the Tribe and on the player’s reputation, so you’d better be ready. Weather in our game is not always as extreme as that; you can also encounter slight drizzles that won't kill you, but will slightly weaken your constructions.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34986580/f530ae7a6f0cae5b56f6e8fe77d59119cae229fa.png[/img]

So with combat or without, surviving on our island won't always be so simple, and we are making sure that there will be many other activities that will help players to fully immerse themselves into the world we are creating.

Until next time!
